# sq-25 — Consumer classification contract

Document and test the descriptor members a downstream classifier relies on to match delimited lab exports against its own declared file types, so a consumer can swap its stand-in describer for squalify. **Not in this slice:** classification itself (a non-goal), new descriptor members unless a gap is found.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-14 architect (B1): squalify follows DataBall's header grammar, prism's ColumnInfo does not: RowID( id ) -> squalify unit id (prism: ' id ', a Unit column); X( ) -> none (prism: Unit ' '); A(b(c)) -> unit 'c)' (prism: none). Recommended: document the grammar and trimming; prism keeps its exact-name checks (D16, D54) on its own parsed header. prism mapping: Id <- nameParenUnit with unit 'id' (ordinal); Unit <- other nameParenUnit; None <- everything else.

## Why

A first consumer (a splitter for lab sweep tables, in another repo) now reads files as describe, classify, transform, split. It ships a small stand-in describer whose output is a subset of this descriptor and will replace it with squalify once delimited profiling exists. Its classifier needs a stable, documented subset; squalify still only describes.

## Files

- `docs/descriptor.md`: a "Consumer subset" section listing the members and their stability under the schema-version policy
- tests on synthetic fixtures under `tests/` (no real files); the private-corpus harness (sq-18) covers real files

## Failing tests

- A synthetic lab sweep table (key columns with an `(id)` unit, `(unit)` measurement columns, unitless setup columns, interleaved all-null separator rows) gives: the dialect and header (sq-04), every header name with its parsed unit convention (sq-14), the row classes with the all-null class (sq-17), and per field `type`, `nulls` and `constant` (sq-05).
- A synthetic one-condition capture table (no key columns, a few varying columns, the rest constant) gives `constant` true for the constant fields and false for the varying ones.
- With values off, a constant field's description says it is constant without revealing the value (`statsWithheld`).
- The consumer-subset members are byte-identical across two runs.

## Implement

- Document how `constant` treats nulls (every non-null value equal) and how a consumer derives "constant with NULL counted as a value" from `constant`, `nulls` and `count`.
